layout: One text sheet in his hand: manuscript number 12 at the top, an opening extension line with an underbrace label and a three-line note at upper right, a fundamental-group display with its own underbrace label, and nineteen prose/formula baselines below the display, ending in a separate final paragraph. There are six interlinear insertions, cancellations, and manuscript number 26 at lower left. The final paragraph continues at the physical bottom without terminal punctuation. The count of 35 includes 21 main baselines, two page numerals, two underbrace labels, three note lines, the separate struck au dessus des line, and six insertion baselines.

changes.math_consequence: Preserves the written subscript delimiters without replacing them by conventional set braces.

Using the coordinate maps written on scan016, rho(z)=1/(1-z) fixes the two roots P and bar-P of z^2-z+1. The three holomorphic involutions z/(z-1),1/z,1-z exchange those roots. Complex conjugation tau also exchanges them. Therefore the stabilizer of either root in S3 x C2 consists of 1,rho,rho^2 and the three sigma_i tau, and has order6. Exact evaluation of all twelve elements in Q(P), P^2-P+1=0, confirms both this subgroup and its complementary six root-exchanging elements. The live list on the page uses the indices1,2,3 instead of the previously defined0,1,infinity; that index change is retained, not silently regularized.

The first fixed-point list has a dotted rho; the later prose writes an undotted rho. Before the first tau, cancellation of the whole rho-squared-like prefix remains preferred, but cancellation of its high2 alone is also possible. As a mathematical check, rho tau has no fixed point: since rho and tau commute, any fixed point would also be fixed by (rho tau)^2=rho^2, hence would be P or bar-P; but rho tau exchanges them. This checks rho tau only; it cannot decide the dark prefix, its high2-like remnant, dot, or cancellation scope. The calculation is not used to choose the ink state.

For sigma_0(z)=z/(z-1), the fixed-point equation is z(z-2)=0. The point0 is a deleted puncture, so2 is its only fixed point in U. Of the six holomorphic transformations, exactly1 and sigma_0 fix2. Tau fixes2 and commutes with both, giving its stabilizer {1,sigma_0,tau,sigma_0 tau}, isomorphic to C2 x C2. The twelve-element exact calculation checks the claimed stabilizer and the number2. The corrected singular wording and undotted sigma_0 are retained as ink decisions.

Conjugating a splitting by a lift of an element carrying P to bar-P gives a splitting over the conjugate stabilizer: for a section s and such a lift t, s'(h)=t s(t^{-1} h t)t^{-1} still projects to h. Replacing t by n t for a kernel element n conjugates the resulting section by n. This checks the stated mechanism and the kernel-conjugacy qualification, conditional on the geometric sections already described; it is not a classification of every maximal partial splitting.

The page's broad correspondence between maximal partial splittings and fixed loci/connected components is carried as its geometric interpretation. The finite-action and extension calculations here do not prove the completeness of that correspondence. The last sentence continues beyond the supplied scan: no continuation or terminal punctuation is invented.
